svg.title: Proof. For a lower bound use the uniform prior on the four labels and give the controller the entire independent erasure schedule in advance. Conditional on that schedule, only N informative trials are available; the ideal uniform-prior Bayes lower bound is eN. Revealing independent schedule information cannot increase the optimum risk, so every original policy’s worst-case risk is at least E[eN]. The proposed policy depends on the successful signs and its initial coin, not on the erased-trial locations or the number of future successful trials. Conditional on the independent schedule it attains eN on every label. This proves the matching upper bound. For common η, the binomial average of 2−N is (1 −η/2)B; correcting its N = 0 and N = 1 terms yields (3). The sequence eN is nonincreasing. Couple success indicators through independent uniforms as Zt = 1{Ut ≤ηt} and Z0 t = 1{Ut ≤η0}. Then N ≥N0 pointwise, so the same policy has risk at most EB(η0). The admitted vector with every efficiency equal to η0 supplies the matching lower bound.
